target_customer: Independent musicians (free tier), with a plan to sell data insights to labels, A&R reps and retailers
problem: Artists lacked a simple view of their social and fan activity across accounts. BeatDeck offered a free dashboard with fans, plays, sentiment and listener behavior.
business_model: Freemium analytics for artists, with planned data licensing to labels and music retailers

founders.name: Josh Mangel
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page; no background found.

founders.name: Avi Zolty
founders.background_notes: Named in the YC page description text and in Crunchbase as co-founder, but the YC founders section lists only Josh Mangel.

competitors.name: Next Big Sound
competitors.what: Music analytics with a free tier and a paid tier of 79 dollars per month
competitors.traction_then: Not stated in the launch article
competitors.funding_then: 6.5 million dollar Series A led by IA Ventures and Foundry Group

technical_complexity.rationale: Aggregating social data across accounts with a sentiment score and listening heatmaps needs API integrations and some data work but no research.

defensibility.rationale: Next Big Sound already offered a free tier and no proprietary data was shown.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Next Big Sound was bought by Pandora in 2015 and shut in 2021. No source ties incumbents to BeatDeck's end.

market_need_then: Artists had social accounts on many platforms and wanted a combined view. Musicmetric and Next Big Sound both raised money in 2012 and 2013, which shows investor interest.

branding.domain_note: beatdeck.com redirected to a domain marketplace listing when fetched.

identity.logo: A logo image appears in the Hypebot launch article, not described by any source

branding.community_and_virality: Hypebot covered the May 2013 launch; no community found.

brand_strength.rationale: A fitting music name with launch coverage, but generic among beat and deck names and no later brand evidence.

outcome_analysis: BeatDeck launched a free artist analytics dashboard in May 2013 against Next Big Sound, which also had a free tier, and Musicmetric. It had a two person team and the only funding found is a 20 thousand dollar seed from YC reported by one database. No shutdown notice or post mortem was found, so the cause is not public. The failure factors are inferences from a free product that planned to monetize data later.
notes: The seed round rests on a single database (CB Insights, 20K on 2013-01-26); Village reports 97K instead. The YC page puts the team in Atlanta while Crunchbase says it was founded in Mountain View. Competitor funding details come from search summaries of 2013 coverage (Musicmetric 4.7M January 2013, Next Big Sound 6.5M Series A, TheNextWeb dated 2013) and the Hypebot launch article names both rivals. The Next Big Sound series A date was reported as early 2012. The cause of inactivity is not public.
